g_roast: Twenty-two years on the floor, and I never saw a crew this bad at standing where they're told, not one.
You lot couldn't organise a piss-up in a brewery, and I've been to some very badly run breweries.
g_fire_back: Give over, love, my old crew said worse than that before the kettle boiled.
That's rich, coming from somebody who hid behind me for the whole of the last fight.
g_pile_on: Aye, and that's the polite version. I watched that one try to put a shield on backwards.
Don't forget the bit where they ran the wrong way. Twice in one fight, that's a skill.
lines.g_peacemake: Right, pack it in, the pair of you. Sit down, shut up, and we'll sort it over a pint.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, I'm with this one. Not taking sides, just telling you what I saw from the front.
lines.g_left_out: You two have got your own thing going. That's fine by me, I'll have a look at the kit.
lines.g_include: Come and sit down, lad, you're making the place look untidy stood there. There's room on the bench.
lines.g_bad_plan: Simple plan for you. I walk in, I stand there, and they all hit me until they get bored and go home.
lines.g_plan_yes: Aye, go on then, I'll go in first. Somebody has to.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that's daft, and you know it's daft. I'm not walking the crew into that.
lines.g_hype: Right, you lot, behind me and stay there. Let's get this shift done.
lines.g_toast: I'm not one for speeches, so this'll be quick. To this lot, who pull their weight. That's all I've got.
lines.g_cheers: Cheers, love, and the first round's mine, so put your money away.
g_quiet_line: Well, that's another shift done. Could've been worse, I suppose.
Somebody's left their kit in a right state, by the way. Not naming names.
lines.g_after_wipe: Right, everyone up, slowly, nobody rushing. We got knocked down, it happens on every floor, so we crack on.
lines.g_crew: I had a crew for twenty-two years, four of us on the floor, and I reckoned that was my lot. Turns out it wasn't.
lines.g_exasperated: I stand at the front so nobody else has to, and every bloody one of you keeps running past me!
lines.g_love_sharp: You say it how it is, no messing. That's how it was on the floor, and I trust it.
lines.g_love_kind: You looked out for me when I didn't ask. Not many do that for the big lad at the front.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, which isn't easy. Little Mick could do it, and you're the first since.
lines.g_love_brave: You don't hang back, not ever. On the floor that's who you wanted next to you on a bad shift.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't flap. When it goes wrong, you just get on with it, and there's no higher praise from a steel floor.
lines.g_love_clever: You work out how things fit together, proper like. Pete was like that with the machines, and I miss it.
lines.g_love_honest: You've never once fed me a line. I can't stand management talk, and you've got none of it.
lines.g_love_quiet: Few words out of you, and fewer out of me. Suits me down to the ground, that.
lines.g_love_fierce: You don't know when you're beaten, and I mean that kindly. I like that in a person, it's a northern thing.
lines.g_love_warm: Being round you feels like the pub on a Friday after a long week. I didn't know I'd been missing that.
g_loved: Give over, love, you'll make me blush, and nobody wants that.
Aye, well, that's nice of you. Don't make a habit of it.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You've always got summat nasty to say. On the floor, a lad like you got put on the night shift, alone.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop fussing over me, love, I'm not made of glass. I'm the one who stands in front, remember?
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything needs a joke. Some things you just shut up and get on with.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in like you've got summat to prove. Somebody always gets hurt cleaning up after a lad like that.
lines.g_hate_steady: You stand there thinking about it while the rest of us get on. At some point you just have to pick up the shovel.
lines.g_hate_clever: You talk to me like I'm thick. I'm not thick, I'm quiet, there's a difference.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say every daft thing that comes into your head. That's not honest, that's just no filter.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never say owt, and then you're surprised when nobody knows what you want. Open your mouth, lad.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a competition with you, even the washing up. It's not a race, it's a shift.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk the hind legs off a donkey, love. Give the rest of us a minute's peace.
lines.g_respect: I don't like you, and I'm not going to pretend. But you pulled your weight back there, and that's what counts.
lines.g_call_out: That one was on you, lad. You ran past me before I'd got set, and look where it got us.
lines.g_stung: Aye, I heard you. I'm going for a walk, don't wait up.
lines.g_concede: You were right, back there, and I've been chewing on it all day. Fair enough, you were right.
lines.g_nod: Aye, and you, you weren't bad. Let's leave it there, eh?
lines.g_callback_save: I haven't forgotten you dragging me up off that floor. I owe you a pint for that, at least.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the only two still standing, and both of us knackered. Best shift I've had in years, that.
lines.g_callback_callout: Last time you had a go at me, I sulked for a full shift. Daft of me, and you were right.
lines.g_former_rivals: When we started, I'd have happily left you out in the rain. Now I'd stand in front of you, no questions.
lines.g_changed: They reckon old dogs don't change. I've talked more this month than I have in years, so maybe they're wrong.
g_unguarded: Right, since it's just us. I fold my hi-vis every night like it's the flag. Don't laugh, it's the only thing I've got from home.
My old crew called me Gentle Dan, after I cried at Little Mick's wedding. If that leaves this table, I'll deny it.
lines.g_clipped: Aye, fine, whatever you reckon. I'll be at the front.
lines.g_noticed_open: Ey up, look who's found their voice. Don't stop on my account, I'm enjoying this.
lines.anchor_notice: You're not the one who first walked in here, you know. I stand at the front, I see who's behind me, and you've changed.
arg_ask: {player}, you sort this out. I've said my bit, and this one's not listening.
Right, {player}, you decide, and we both shut up about it. That fair enough for you?
lines.arg_backed_me: Ta for that, {player}. Knew you'd see sense in the end.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fair enough, your call. I still think it's daft, but I'll crack on.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Keeping out of it? Can't blame you, love, I would too.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Them again, {player}. Every single time, and I've stopped being surprised by it.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's going to call it, so I will. I'm right, and that's the end of it.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, not having it. I've seen how that ends from the front.
lines.arg_grumble: Still reckon I had that one right. Not going on about it, just saying.
lines.arg_settled: Right, we're both half daft. Shake on it and let's get a pint.
lines.seen_listens: You let a man get to it in his own time, {player}. Not many do that for the quiet ones.
lines.seen_truth: You tell it straight, {player}, no management talk. I can work with that.
lines.seen_jokes: When it all goes to pot, you've a joke ready, {player}. My old crew was the same, and it got us through.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep your nose out of everybody's rows, {player}. Wish I'd had your sense, I'd have had a quieter life.
lines.seen_biased: There's one you favour, love, and the whole crew can see it. Just saying, that's all.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be hard on folk, {player}. Me, I've had worse off a foreman, but some of this lot haven't.
lines.seed_right: Them words of yours after the mess, {player}. Got right on my nerves at the time. Today I did it your way, and it worked.
lines.seed_remember: Still chewing on them words of yours from when it went wrong. Haven't decided owt yet.
lines.seed_wrong: Did it your way, {player}, and it went worse. Just so you know.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Have you a minute, {player}? That one was close, closer than I'd say in front of the others.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all got flattened back there. Sit down a minute, I want to go through what happened.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} went down first, and I was meant to be in front. Something got past me, and nowt gets past me.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, start to finish, everyone walking. That's a proper shift, that, so the first round's on me.
lines.talk_development: Odd question, {player}. Have I changed? The lads on the floor always said I'd never change, and now I'm not sure.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been short with {name}. Not everybody grew up on a steel floor, and I forget that.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Honest answer, {player}. Does {name} rate me, or am I just the big lad who stands in front?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: Can't stand {name}, {player}, never could. But I'd want them on my crew if it went bad, and that annoys me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Summat's not right with {name}. They've gone quiet, and not their usual quiet.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: A word, {player}. The good kit always ends up with {name}, every trip, without fail. I'm not daft, and nor's anybody else.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll say it to your face, that's how I was raised. Me and {name} don't get on, and I've given up acting like we do.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep marching into places we've no business being, {player}. I'll take the front against owt, but not against stupidity.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: It's {name}, love. Their call was right and mine wasn't, and I'd rather tell you before I go back to being stubborn.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust me, {player}? When the real graft comes, I'm sat in the pub while the rest of you go out.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit went to {name} and nobody said a word. I'd have passed it over myself, love, if anybody had asked.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Aye, that does help, that. Ta very much, {player}.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be all right. Always am, give it a day.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Right, not what I needed to hear, that. I'll go for a walk.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you've noticed it too. Good, makes it easier.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Could be, could be not. We'll see how it goes.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it, love. You've got hold of the wrong end.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair enough, then. I'll have a word with {name}, proper like.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Maybe, maybe not. People are a mystery to me, always have been.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I mentioned it. And not a word to {name}, right?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, that, fair enough. I'm a bit narked yet, but it'll pass.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Aye, I heard you. I'll chew it over.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, so that's how it is. Good to know, {player}.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, that's me done with this one. I'll be at the front if you want me.

history.open: I worked a steel floor for twenty-two years, {player}, four of us on a crew. Gaz, Little Mick, Pete and me.

options.reply: Hot, loud, and you'd trust the lad next to you with your life every shift. Nobody said so, mind. You'd sound soft.
Six foot four, love. That's Sheffield for you, nobody's ever called what they are.
Every Friday, about half six. That's when we'd go for a pint, nine years straight.

history.open: Landed in Durotar in my hi-vis, {player}. First week on a new job, driving a forklift in a warehouse. I'd only just got the vest.

options.reply: Fold it every night. Daft, I know. It's the last bit of being useful back home, and I'm keeping hold of it.

options.text: At least the orcs could see you coming.
options.reply: Ha, they could, from a mile off. Didn't stop them asking if I was a very bright sort of goblin.

history.open: Our Jade's a paramedic, {player}, or she was, in Leeds. She married a lad called Dawson the year before all this. So she's a Dawson on the lists now.

options.reply: About forty times, every hub. Alphabetical, they are, so I go straight to the D's and then the O's, just in case.

options.text: A paramedic. She'll be out there helping people.
options.reply: Aye, she will. That's what I tell myself. She's tougher than me, always was.

friend.open: When the plant shut, {player}, I spent four years on the sofa. Stopped answering the phone. Our Jade came round every Sunday and made me eat. I've never told her what that did for me.

options.text: You'll get the chance to tell her.
options.reply: Hope so, love. First pint I buy her, that's what I'm saying. Then I'll go quiet again, she'll be used to that.
Aye, well, there it is. Seemed like you ought to know why I won't sit still. Don't go spreading it.

sworn.open: On the floor, you didn't say you cared about your crew, {player}. You just never let owt past you to them. You're crew now. That's the most I've got to say.

options.reply: Aye, well, give over before I get something in my eye.
It's meant to. Now let's get a pint before this turns into a speech.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} had it out, properly. We're sorted now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Give over, love. But aye, it's good.
I did, obviously. That's how you know it's sorted in Sheffield.
